newsitem.title: USA: Reno promises San Francisco marijuana club review.
newsitem.headline: Reno promises San Francisco marijuana club review.

text.p: U.S. Attorney General Janet Reno on Thursday promised a careful review of a recently reopened San Francisco club that supplies marijuana to the sick.

"As I have indicated with respect to that whole issue, we will be looking at each case. We will review the evidence on a case-by-case basis and make an appropriate determination," she said at the weekly Justice Department news briefing.

California voters in November approved a measure that allows sick people and their "primary caregiver" to legally possess and grow marijuana for medical use when recommended by a doctor. Under federal law, marijuana is still illegal.

Reno was asked repeatedly whether the federal government would send agents to arrest those who go to the San Francisco Cannabis Cultivators' Club, which won approval from a local judge to reopen in accordance with the new state measure.
"One of the issues that we have got to address is what is the state role, what is the circumstance with respect to the court order, any of the conditions of the court order," Reno said.
"And we have got to move through it carefully and look at it -- based on the evidence and the law, the role of the state of California and the application of federal law," she said.
Reno acknowledged the federal government has limited resources and must focus on cases that have a significant impact.
Within a few hours on Wednesday after reopening, the club's founder Dennis Peron said it had given out about 700 applications for membership and 200 people had already bought marijuana.
